pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should you do first before filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Read all the instructions
   B. Fill any box
   C. Fold it
   D. Sign

2. Which sentence belongs to the main idea Fire is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. Never play with matches.
   B. The market is far.
   C. Rain is wet.
   D. Maize is tasty.

3. What does the proverb Look before you leap advise a writer of a story about a careless pupil? (1 mark)
   A. Be careless
   B. Never look
   C. Think before acting
   D. Run fast

4. What is extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Reading many books widely for pleasure
   B. Copying a book
   C. Reading only the title
   D. Reading one word only

5. What is polite when you want to speak in a discussion? (1 mark)
   A. Snatch the talking stick
   B. Shout
   C. Stand on a chair
   D. Raise your hand or signal

6. What do we do in a matching game with words? (1 mark)
   A. Count the cards
   B. Sing a song
   C. Match each word with its meaning
   D. Draw a picture only

7. What is leisure time? (1 mark)
   A. Free time when you are not working or in class
   B. Lesson time
   C. Exam time
   D. Sleeping time

8. What is a good response when you did not understand an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
   B. Guess quietly
   C. Leave
   D. Do anything

9. What should you not do with an advert that asks for money from strangers? (1 mark)
   A. Send money without asking an adult
   B. Check the facts
   C. Ask an adult
   D. Read it carefully

10. What does Asiyesikia la mkuu huvunjika guu teach? (1 mark)
   A. Never walk
   B. Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   C. Legs are weak
   D. Elders are always wrong

11. What is reader's theatre? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing lesson
   B. A reading test
   C. Acting with costumes only
   D. Reading a script aloud with different parts

12. What is the subject of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. What is said about it
   B. The verb only
   C. Who or what the sentence is about
   D. The full stop

13. What does format mean for a form? (1 mark)
   A. Who wrote it
   B. How old it is
   C. How it is arranged on the page
   D. What it costs

14. Which word means not inside? (1 mark)
   A. beside
   B. between
   C. outside
   D. under

15. What should a newsreader do? (1 mark)
   A. Speak clearly at a steady pace
   B. Skip words
   C. Mumble
   D. Shout

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Give three questions you can ask when studying a picture. (3 marks)

17. Explain how you would perform a choral poem with your class. Include voice, pace and non-verbal cues. (5 marks)

18. Name three headings in a story plan. (3 marks)

19. Give two conjunctions used to join sentences. (2 marks)

20. Explain what an interjection is and give two examples. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Read all the instructions
   Reading first prevents mistakes.

2. A — Never play with matches.
   It is a detail about fire safety.

3. C — Think before acting
   It would fit a story where carelessness causes trouble.

4. A — Reading many books widely for pleasure
   Extensive reading means reading a lot for enjoyment.

5. D — Raise your hand or signal
   Signal politely.

6. C — Match each word with its meaning
   The game links words to meanings.

7. A — Free time when you are not working or in class
   Leisure is free time.

8. A — Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
   Polite questions help you understand.

9. A — Send money without asking an adult
   Never send money to strangers.

10. B — Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   It means one who does not listen to the elders may come to harm.

11. D — Reading a script aloud with different parts
   Pupils read parts with expression.

12. C — Who or what the sentence is about
   The subject is the topic of the sentence.

13. C — How it is arranged on the page
   Format is the layout.

14. C — outside
   Outside means not inside.

15. A — Speak clearly at a steady pace
   Clear speech helps listeners.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who is there, where are they, what are they doing, why, what happens next.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: Learn the poem well, keep the same pace together, speak clearly with expression, use gestures and smiles as non-verbal cues, look at the audience and practise beforehand.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of five points.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each heading.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: and, but, or, so (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: An interjection is a short word or sound showing sudden feeling, for example Wow and Ouch.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for two examples.
